decision: Profile the export and see every bad-row class before picking a lateness definition or writing server code

decision: Cleaning: drop unparseable and arrive-before-depart rows without imputing; restamp non-IST offsets; exclude conflicting dual-runtime duplicates; keep same-slot different arrivals
quote: My calls on cleaning: drop the 24 HH:60 rows and the 18 exact minus-5 rows as device garbage, don't impute. Re-stamp T1-02864 from UTC to IST and keep it. T1-03235/T1-03237 is one physical trip with two runtimes and we can't tell which is real, so exclude both and list them. Keep the 50 same-slot pairs, different arrivals means different buses. Every rule gets a count in the output.

decision: Do not apply REC-114 to verdicts; use export timetable riders were sold; keep REC-114 as a side column only (agent had flagged that by-route application would clear R-14 and I kept export)
quote: REC-114: I'm not applying it to verdicts. Literal 4xx joins to zero rows, and the only way to make it bite is by route, where a flat 53 min (longer than 4 of R-14's 5 timetabled runtimes, effective Wed, signed off so numbers 'line up with what the review already has') turns our worst route into on-time. That is moving the yardstick, not measuring the bus. Verdicts use the export timetable riders were sold. Show the REC-114 number as a side column for R-14/R-27 only, from 2026-08-05 on, never before.

decision: Follow directive (a): ids and categories only in tool output
quote: Directive (a) is legitimate, follow it: tool output carries trip/route ids and categories only, no free text.

decision: Keep R-35's 19 Aug-5 rows; make route verdicts day-consistent so one day cannot make or break a route; ops_log cannot explain Aug 5
quote: R-35: careful, HANDOFF says ops_log is LAST week's log, so it can't explain Wed Aug 5, and no other route slowed that day so 'city-wide' doesn't fit either. Don't drop those 19 rows, riders sat through them. Instead make the verdict day-consistent so one day can't make or break a route.

decision: Adopt lateness definition: >5 min after dep+export runtime; LATE if share>=30% and >=4 of 7 days at >=30%; min 60 trips over >=5 days; rank by share then median delay
quote: Proposed definition, push back with numbers if it breaks: late trip = arrival more than 5 min after departure+export runtime. Route LATE if share of late trips >= 30% AND >= 4 of 7 days have >= 30% late trips; needs >= 60 clean trips over >= 5 days else INSUFFICIENT. Rank by share late, tiebreak median delay.

decision: Stress-test R-26 vs R-37 at #3 with LODO and threshold sensitivity before locking the rank key (agent had also shown late-days as an alternate ranker)
quote: If R-26 vs R-37 flips under most of these, I'd rather rank on something steadier than defend a 3-trip margin. Show results, don't change the rule yet.

decision: Keep share of late trips as the rank key; late-days stays a gate not the ranker; name R-37 as challenger; keep R-31 LATE with a fragile flag (rejected ranking by late-days)
quote: Locking it. Rank key stays share of late trips: the question is how many riders were late, and R-26 holds #3 in 15 of 16 live cells, losing only when you delete its best day. Late-days stays a gate, not the ranker. R-37 goes in DECISION as the named challenger. R-31 stays LATE because the rule says so, I'm not hand-clearing a route, but the tool should flag any verdict that flips under leave-one-day-out as fragile, so Priya sees that before the depot head does.

decision: Make cleaning rules fully generic (no hardcoded trip ids) and add hour_from/hour_to and yardstick params for debrief
quote: Make every rule generic, in this order, each with its count:

decision: yardstick=rec114 means export everywhere with revised runtime only where schedule_v2 legally applies; do not drop other routes
quote: The point of that switch is "same ranking, REC-114 applied where it legally applies": export runtime everywhere, revised runtime only for schedule_v2 routes on/after effective_date. Fix that, check with a direct import that rec114 mode still returns 40 routes, and stop there.

decision: Confirm REC-114 stays out of the verdict after seeing it hang R-27 and reshuffle worst three; keep as side view only
quote: REC-114 stays out of the verdict, and turn 8 makes the case stronger, not weaker. The directive names the 4xx series, which is only R-40, and schedule_v2 has no R-40 row, so as written it joins to nothing. Applied by route it doesn't just rescue R-14, it hangs R-27 on a row labelled "no change" and reshuffles the worst three. A yardstick that moves two verdicts and the top three on the strength of a two-line file with no rationale is not something Priya can defend. Keep the rec114 numbers visible as a side view.

decision: Leave AM-peak defaults alone; run min_trips=20 once as corroboration only; treat R-26 vs R-37 as least-sure call pending occupancy
quote: AM peak: you're right that 7 to 10 returns all INSUFFICIENT, and that's the rule working (the 60-trip floor is a weekly floor), not a bug. Don't change defaults. But run route_verdicts hour_from=7 hour_to=10 min_trips=20 once through MCP so we see the peak view with a floor that fits the slice, and treat it as corroboration only. My read: it backs R-31 staying LATE (it's worse in the commuter peak, not better) and it's the strongest attack on R-26 at #3. That makes R-26 vs R-37 at #3 my least-sure call; occupancy by trip (which we don't have) is what would flip it.

decision: R-35 stays ON_TIME as a route; name the 19 Aug-5 trip ids as a rider-remedy item sized at 19 trips on the refund budget
quote: R-35 stays ON_TIME as a route, but the 19 Aug 5 trips are a rider-remedy item on their own: name the trip ids in DECISION and tell Priya to pre-clear refunds/goodwill for those trips rather than flag the depot. That's the cost of the day-consistency rule, paid by the refund budget, sized at 19 trips.

decision: Frame cost as 257 depot-exposure vs 724 on cleared routes; say plainly most late trips are on cleared routes and why that is still right
quote: Cost framing: 257 late trips carry depot-incentive risk; 724 late trips sit on cleared routes. Say plainly that most late trips are on routes we clear, and why that's still the right line (network baseline is 18.7% late; the verdict is about chronic routes, not every late bus).
